scenes.title: It only works if it remembers you.
scenes.caption: The deal every assistant asks you to make.
scenes.narration: An assistant is only useful if it remembers you. Where you live. Who your doctor is. When the house is empty.

scenes.title: So where does that live?
scenes.caption: Most people quietly stop telling it the truth.
scenes.narration: And all of that gets remembered on a machine you will never see. So most people quietly stop telling it the truth.

scenes.title: Companion Memory
scenes.caption: A home for your digital memory.
scenes.narration: Other agents are double agents. Companion Memory works only for you.

scenes.caption: Your life creates context every day.
scenes.narration: Your life already leaves a trail, across two dozen services that each keep a piece of it.

shots.alt: Two dozen service marks — Gmail, Google Drive, Dropbox, WhatsApp, Instagram, Spotify, Steam, GitHub and the rest — orbiting the Companion Intelligence mark on threads that run into it.
shots._focusNote:
NOT A CAPTURE. This plate is Companion Intelligence's own artwork from ci.computer/memory (`CI-graphic-CollectDigitalTraces`), composited onto the kit's ground colour #041620 at each viewport's native plate size — 3840x2160 and 1080x1920 — so it is never stretched out of its 1:1 aspect. It lives under assets/shots/ because `shotPath` is the only full-frame image slot the grammar has; see video/README.md § 'The two graphic plates' and the GRAPHIC_SHOTS list in video/make.sh, which excludes it from the capture-pass guard for that reason.

focus is the full plate (w 1, h 1) ON PURPOSE: that asks for coverScale exactly, which drops the browser card and its chrome and makes the artwork the frame from the first frame to the last. A graphic wearing browser chrome would read as a screenshot of a web page, which it is not. drift-down rather than push-in for the same reason — with `focus` a push-in STARTS at rest, i.e. on the card, and this shot must never show one. At coverScale there is no headroom to drift, so the kit degrades it to an 8% push and says so in the build log; that is the intended move, not a fallback.

The subject is composed into the upper 74% of both plates because the caption scrim owns roughly the bottom quarter of a full-bleed frame.

scenes.caption: Your accounts, pulled into your own box.
scenes.narration: Point it at the accounts you already have, and it pulls your mail, your calendar and your photos into your own house.

shots.alt: The onboarding connect-source step, offering providers, the browser extension and the import tools
shots._focusNote:
The first product frame in the film, and the first thing that has to stop looking like the two title cards before it. At rest this shot is the fleet's default composition — a browser window floating on a dark field — and the craft audit counted 21 of 30 sampled frames in the old cut as exactly that. So the move ends full-bleed on the provider grid: the Microsoft, Google and Meta cards are the only saturated colour anywhere in this product, and at 1.5x they fill the frame with four blocks of blue, violet and green. It is the largest single change of register in the cut and it is bought with a rectangle, not a re-shoot.

The rectangle keeps the 'Pull your email and calendar in automatically' sub-heading and the whole top row INCLUDING each card's caption line, because those captions are what verifies the narration: Google's reads 'Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Photos, and YouTube', which is the sentence's 'mail, calendar and photos' printed on screen. Framing tighter on the logos alone would have made the line unsupported by its own frame.

LANDSCAPE ONLY, and re-tested rather than inherited. The original reason given was that a portrait rectangle 'could only ask for full-bleed', which is not true — the portrait floor is a 0.738 window, tighter than full-bleed. It was tried: at 1.889x the frame slices the 'Connect a source' heading through the middle of the type and clips both ends of the sub-heading ('Pull' loses its P). Loosening to a 0.87 window keeps the type intact but drops the Microsoft card's caption line — 'Bring your Microsoft account into the mix for email and scheduling', the portrait cut's only printed proof of the narration's 'mail, your calendar' — into the bleed scrim, which is captionAllowance x 2.6 = 772px of a 1920 canvas. So the conclusion stands even though the stated reason did not. Portrait gets the tap instead.

POINTER. The line is 'Point it at the accounts you already have', and a provider card is the control that does it. Landscape lands on the Google card (0.500, 0.372) — verified dead centre of the Google mark, and inside the move's end window (0.688 of the plate from (0.055, 0.013)) — because Google's is the caption the rectangle was chosen to keep. Portrait lands on the Microsoft card (0.500, 0.433), verified centre of the Microsoft mark: on a phone the cards stack full-width and Microsoft's is the only one wholly on the plate. Both are taps/clicks on a card, not on a logo — the logo is just where the card's centre is.

scenes.caption: One list. Every kind of thing you keep.
scenes.narration: Everything you keep lands in one list, on one machine, newest first.

shots.alt: The memory explorer list view, grouped by date
shots._focusNote:
Deliberately the ONLY wide read in the second half of the film, and deliberately un-focused. The scene after it is a punch-in on one row of this exact list, and a crop only reads as a crop if the audience has seen the whole thing first — the same establish-then-punch pair the old cut had, kept because it was the one piece of camera grammar it got right.

POINTER, and it is the load-bearing one in this film. The establish-then-punch pair was always two screenshots that happen to be of the same screen; a cursor makes it cause and effect. The row it lands on is 'Pizza Night' — the first row, which is what 'newest first' names — and the shot in the NEXT scene is that row's record: memory-detail-sheet is titled 'Pizza Night' in BOTH plates, because its capture recipe is this shot's plus `click: div[role="button"] >> nth=0`. So the click is not a decoration over a still: it is the exact interaction that produced the following frame, and the `cut` between the two scenes is now motivated rather than merely fast.

That recipe is also why a row counts as a control here — it is literally `div[role="button"]`, and this shot's own `waitFor` is that selector.

Coordinates verified against the plates: landscape (0.26, 0.163) sits on the words 'Pizza Night'; portrait (0.35, 0.270) sits between the title and 'Homemade pizza night.'. Neither shot has a focus rectangle, so the whole plate is on screen for the whole scene and neither hotspot can drift out of frame.

`at` is 3.3s of a 4.80s fitted window (69%, against the 58% default) so the ring is still resolving as the cut lands. The kit's own bound is 4.20s, so there is 0.9s of slack if a re-recorded line shortens the scene; past that it clamps and warns rather than clicking off the end.

scenes.caption: Open a row and the whole record is there.
scenes.narration: Open one, and the whole record is there. The place, the address, the exact coordinates.

shots.alt: The entity details sheet open over the list, showing one event's full record
shots._focusNote:
The narration names three field values — 'The place, the address, the exact coordinates' — and until this change the ADDRESS was the one the frame cut. Measured off the rendered landscape cut (video-kit 0.24.0, origin/main @ 208a6410, t=44.0s) and off `ci-video focus-preview --at end`: the old 0.576 window from (0.224, 0.112) ends at plate x 0.800, and the address value runs to about 0.892, so the end frame read '4 Sanctuary Ridge, Laguna' and stopped mid-word on the one line the sentence promises. A caption cannot be true of a value the push-in amputates.

0.625 from (0.313, 0.100) — scale 2.065, down from 2.240 — reaches plate x 0.938 and carries '4 Sanctuary Ridge, Laguna Beach, CA 92651' whole with margin, while PLACE, COORDINATES and TYPE stay above the caption band and the Details block stays on screen. It is LESS zoom than before, not more: the rectangle was mis-aimed, not too tight.

The left edge still falls inside the list underneath and a few dimmed row subtitles are cut mid-word. That is unchanged and still unavoidable at any usable scale — excluding the list entirely needs a window of 0.48 and the ceiling is 0.526 — and it reads as depth behind the sheet rather than as damage, because the sheet dims everything under it. Flagged rather than hidden.

SIDE EFFECT WORTH KNOWING, and it is a mitigation rather than a fix: `capture.mask` paints the sheet's `<time>` elements with `color.card`, which renders as a column of nine identical teal pills down the sheet's right gutter (plate x 0.945-0.974) — indistinguishable from a loading skeleton in an otherwise fully painted page. This window ends at 0.938, so the pills are out of the END frame; they are still there at the start of the push. The real fix is the one hazard 4 in capture.config.mjs already reached for the forecast strip — hide the element rather than paint a rectangle over it — and it needs a re-capture against the full stage, so it is filed there, not faked here.

Portrait is a full-bleed reframe, not a crop: mobile stacks this record full-width, so w 1.0 asks for coverScale, the phone frame drops away and the record grows 39%. Unchanged.

scenes.caption: Search runs on the box. Nothing is uploaded.
scenes.narration: Search it, and the whole store narrows in place. Nothing is uploaded, and nothing leaves the box.

shots.alt: The memory explorer filtered down to results matching coffee
shots._focusNote:
The only pull-back in the film, and the reason it is here rather than anywhere else: this is the one beat whose sentence has a direction. The shot OPENS tight enough that the query 'coffee' in the search field and the first six matched rows are legible, then reveals the rest of the store around them — the answer first, the haystack second, which is the order the line asks a question in.

The rectangle starts at x 0.17 so the left nav rail and the year-heatmap column stay out of the opening frame; they are furniture, and at 1.5x they would be the first thing read. max(w,h) is 0.83, which puts the opening scale at about 1.55x — comfortably inside MAX_SCALE, so the rectangle is honoured rather than clamped, and a pull-back that starts at a clamped scale is a pull-back from somewhere the author did not choose.

PORTRAIT NOW HAS THE SAME BEAT. The old note said the phone capture has 'no separate search column to open on' — true, but it does not need one: the mobile plate carries a full-width search field with 'coffee' in it at the very top, above the List/Map/Gallery/Graph tabs. Without a rectangle this shot resolved to the legacy pull-back mirror, scale 1.045 -> 1.0 over 6.63s, which is the 0.75%/second the kit calls below the threshold of noticing — the portrait cut's most static shot. The rectangle asks for a 0.797 window anchored to the plate's top-left (the translate clamps, so the reported origin is (0.002, -0.002)), which opens on the query and six matched rows at 1.749x and then reveals the store. A 0.738 window — the portrait floor — was tried first and cut the search field off the top of the opening frame entirely, which would also have put the tap below on nothing.

POINTER: the search field itself, which is the control the line names ('Search it, and the whole store narrows in place'). Landscape (0.760, 0.037) is verified on the word 'coffee' inside the input; portrait (0.170, 0.047) likewise. `at` is 2.0s of a 6.63s window rather than the 58% default, because a click that lands after the reveal has the causality backwards — the click is what narrows the store, so it happens while the frame is still tight. It is late enough that the opening window has already widened past its tightest, which keeps the landscape hotspot (0.039 of the plate from the opening window's right edge) clear of the frame edge with room to spare.

scenes.caption: People, places and ideas — connected on your hardware.
scenes.narration: It works out how your people, places and ideas connect — on your box, not somebody else's cluster.

shots.alt: The memory explorer graph view, hop-depth and neighbour controls above the force graph
shots._focusNote:
At rest this is another window on a dark field and the node labels are unreadable. The rectangle frames the core of the constellation — John Smith and the first ring of people and topics around him — at 2.398x, which is where the labels become words instead of texture. The rectangle's centre is (0.44, 0.392) — chosen off the plate, not from the geometric middle, because that is what puts John Smith and his first ring in the window this seed actually produced. (The previous note said (0.55, 0.49) and 'about 2.2x'; neither matched the numbers in the file, so both are corrected here rather than left to be trusted.)

MOTION CHANGED, push-in -> drift-down, as half of a swap with it-notices; the other half and the measurement that forced it are written up there. Two things make this the good half of the trade rather than the price of it. First, the rectangle is now where the shot STARTS: the names are legible from frame one instead of arriving at the end, which matters for a beat whose claim is that the box worked out how your people connect — you cannot read a claim about names off a frame with no readable names. Second, a force graph is a field, and a camera travelling down through it is reading it, the same argument the insights column made for itself. The travel is real and was checked for the drift-down-with-no-room trap: 127px landscape at 2.398x, 162px portrait at 1.889x, no degradation reported by cameraMove in either format, and John Smith stays in frame from the first frame to the last.

THIS SHOT DRIFTS BETWEEN RE-SEEDS. The force graph has no fixed layout, so the node positions move on any re-capture and this rectangle points at a slightly different part of the cloud each time — video/README.md lists it as one of the two documented drift shots. It is framed loosely enough (0.58 of the plate) to survive that; a tighter crop on one named node would be a rectangle that silently rots.

PORTRAIT NOW HAS ONE TOO. 'The mobile graph is already near-full-width' was about the plate, not about the frame: the plate is near-full-width, but at rest the plate is presented inside a 772px phone frame on a 1080px canvas, so without a rectangle this shot was the legacy 1.045 creep and every node label was texture. The rectangle asks for the portrait floor — a 0.738 window at the resolution ceiling, 1.889x — centred on (0.55, 0.465), which is where this seed's cloud actually sits. Checked on a reconstructed end frame: every label from Cooking to Architecture is a word, nothing is clipped ('Documentary' is the closest to an edge and clears it), and the cloud lands in the upper 63% of the canvas, i.e. above the bleed scrim. Loose framing is the drift insurance here as in landscape — 0.738 is the loosest tight frame portrait can produce, so a re-seed has the whole margin to move in.

No pointer: the caption and narration name people, places and ideas, not a control, and the hop-depth and neighbour controls this shot's `before` step scrolls past are not on either plate.

before.eval: () => { const HEADER = 64; const s = [...document.querySelectorAll('svg')].sort((a, b) => b.getBoundingClientRect().height - a.getBoundingClientRect().height)[0]; if (!s) return; const r = s.getBoundingClientRect(); const d = Math.max(0, r.top - HEADER); if (d < 1) return; let el = s.parentElement; while (el && !(/(auto|scroll)/.test(getComputedStyle(el).overflowY) && el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1)) el = el.parentElement; if (el) el.scrollTop += d; }

scenes.caption: It reads what happened and writes it up.
scenes.narration: Hourly, daily, weekly — it reads what happened and writes the summary itself, on a model you host.

shots.alt: The insights and summaries page, listing the daily and weekly summaries it generated
shots._focusNote:
The claim is that the appliance NOTICED something, so the frame has to show a thing it noticed rather than a page of cards. The rectangle lands on the first two summaries, which puts 'Oil change due soon for your Honda Accord (last service ~4,900 miles ago)' at a size a viewer can actually read — and that sentence is the whole argument for this beat.

MOTION CHANGED, drift-down -> push-in, SWAPPED WITH it-connects, which takes the drift-down. This is the one place authorial decisions were overturned rather than extended, so here is the measurement that forced it and why the swap is the cheap way out.

Resolving every shot through the kit's own cameraMove shows drift-down was this film's most-repeated verb — 3 of 9 shots — and that two of the three were ADJACENT: this scene and how-it-works. It is worse than a coincidence of verbs: your-traces and how-it-works resolve to BYTE-IDENTICAL moves in both formats (landscape scale 1.613, y 97.903 -> 12.446; portrait 1.743, y 199.913 -> 50.468), because they are the same kind of plate framed the same way, so the film already spends three shots on one move. how-it-works cannot be the one that changes: it is a full-bleed graphic, and push-in starts at rest while pull-back ends there, either of which puts the browser card on screen — the one thing a graphic plate must never show — and hold is frozen picture. With scene 8 locked to drift, scene 7 cannot be drift. That is arithmetic, not taste.

That left push-in or pull-back here. Both were resolved and compared. Pull-back keeps this shot's legible frame at the start but ends on a browser window on a dark field, and it-connects would still OPEN on one — two exposures to the composition the whole rework is fighting. Swapping instead moves the drift onto it-connects, which then opens bleeding at 2.398x and never shows the card at all, so the count of shots that touch the default composition is unchanged at one. Perfect alternation falls out of it: drift, push, drift, push, pull, drift, push, drift, push, with no adjacent repeat in either format.

The rectangle is untouched, so nothing the drift-down note fought for is lost — the two cards at 1.875x are now where the shot ARRIVES rather than where it opens. The cost, stated plainly: the first second or so of this shot is the fleet-default composition. It is paid for by it-connects no longer having the same problem.

PORTRAIT RECTANGLE ADDED. Without one this shot was the legacy drift, an 86px translate with no scale change. The rectangle asks for a 0.897 window; the top edge was tuned by preview until it fell in the gap ABOVE the first card rather than through 'Insights & Summaries' (y 0.10 sliced the heading; y 0.13 clears it), and the width was opened from 0.738 to 0.90 because at the floor the card body text ran off both edges — 'Home & Car Upkeep' lost its margin and 'on the road:' lost its colon. Both cards now sit whole, with the Honda Accord line legible, which is the same argument as landscape.

THE LINE NAMES THE CADENCE THE FRAME SHOWS, and it took a correction to get there. It read 'Overnight it reads your week' — but the two cards this rectangle frames are both badged HOURLY, so the frame was showing one thing while the voice named another. `backend/apps/summary/src/system_schedules.py` registers three: hourly at `5 * * * *`, daily at `10 0 * * *`, weekly at `15 0 * * MON`. The line now names all three, which is true of the product AND of the two badges in shot.

Who writes these: `summary-service` is a container in this appliance's own compose stack (docker-compose.yml), pointed at the LLM endpoint configured in Settings -> Model, which defaults to Ollama on the host gateway. Hence 'a model you host' rather than 'a model on this machine' — the default is the same box, but the setting can name another one you run, and the narration should be true of both.

scenes.caption: Input surfaces. Digital memory. Your agents.
scenes.narration: Underneath it is one shape. Raw data in; people, places, things and events out.

shots.alt: Companion Intelligence's architecture diagram: INPUT SURFACES (devices, API plug-ins, native apps, browser) feeding DIGITAL MEMORY (raw data, normalized shapes, database, the user's RL model, insights), feeding AGENTS (Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, NanoClaw, Claude, Codex) under UNIVERSAL MCP SUPPORT.
shots._focusNote:
NOT A CAPTURE — the same arrangement as `graphic-traces`, and the same reasons. This is the explainer from the 2026 Q3 Companion Intelligence short deck, the one ci.computer/memory publishes under 'How does Companion Memory work?'. It is composited on #041620 at 3840x2160 and 1080x1920 rather than scaled into the 16:9 shot slot, because the source is 2500x1236 (2.02:1) and the slot would have stretched it.

THE CAPTION NAMES THE THREE PANELS, SO THE FRAME HAS TO END ON THEM. At 0.8 from (0, 0) the drift-down ended with its window top at plate y 0.107, and the three panel headings sit at 0.086-0.104 — so the last frame of a nine-second scene sliced INPUT SURFACES, DIGITAL MEMORY and AGENTS in half, horizontally, through the glyphs, under a caption reading 'Input surfaces. Digital memory. Your agents.' The same rectangle cut UNIVERSAL MCP SUPPORT to 'UNIV / MCP S' at the right edge in landscape, and AGENTS to 'AGENT' in portrait.

Measured with `ci-video focus-preview --at start` and `--at end` at both viewports. drift-down puts its window top at (requested y + a fixed inset) + half the drift, so on this plate the END is always LOWER than the start and there is no y that keeps the headings at a window of 0.8 — the fix has to be a wider window, which shortens the drift. 0.94 from (0.05, 0) lands the landscape end at 0.083, above the headings, and reaches plate x 0.99 so the AGENTS panel and UNIVERSAL MCP SUPPORT are whole. 0.92 from (0.04, 0) does the same in portrait with margin on both sides.

pull-back was tried and rejected on measurement, not taste: it ends at the plate's natural size, which is legible in landscape and reduces the portrait diagram to roughly a third of its current height, where the box labels stop reading. `motion` is one enum for both formats, so a move that only works in one is not available.

WHAT EACH VIEWPORT CAN ACTUALLY READ, because the line has to be true of both: in landscape the whole diagram is legible down to the box labels — PERSON, PLACE, THING, CONTENT, EVENT, SPACE and FT SEARCH / RELATIONS / GRAPH / VECTOR, which is exactly what the narration names. In portrait the plate is 1060px wide and the three panel headings plus the box labels still read, but the smallest type is texture. The caption names the three panels for that reason: it is the claim both cuts can carry — and now both cuts carry it at the end of the shot as well as the start.

EXPECTED BUILD LINE, so nobody 'fixes' it: at 0.94 the landscape window leaves less headroom than the drift needs, and the kit says so and pushes in instead — `! scene "how-it-works" shot "graphic-architecture" (landscape): drift-down had no room at this focus — pushed in instead`. That fallback is the point. It gives landscape a start at the plate's natural size and an end at 0.94 from (0.049, 0.052), both with the headings whole; portrait keeps a real drift-down, 0.055 to 0.082, also with the headings whole at both ends. Writing `motion: "push-in"` explicitly would silence the line and take portrait with it — `motion` is one enum for both formats — and a portrait push-in STARTS at 1.394x the plate, where the diagram is about a third of its readable height. `ci-video check` passes with 0 errors either way; the warning is the kit reporting a decision, not a defect.

scenes.title: Universal MCP support
scenes.caption: The agents you already use, on a memory that is yours.
scenes.narration: Which is why the agents you already use plug straight into it, over one MCP server that answers only to you.

scenes.caption: Cautious, balanced, or hands off. You choose.
scenes.narration: How much it does on its own is a dial you set. Cautious, balanced, or hands off.

shots.alt: The onboarding trust dial, offering cautious, balanced and hands-off
shots._focusNote:
THE LINE NAMES THREE OPTIONS AND THE FRAME HAS TO HOLD THREE. The previous rectangle did not, and the note it replaces claimed the opposite, so this one carries the measurement.

Read off the rendered landscape cut (video-kit 0.24.0, origin/main @ 208a6410): at t=79.0s, the shot at rest, all three cards are legible. By t=82.5s — the last 2.5s of the scene, over a caption reading 'Cautious, balanced, or hands off. You choose.' — the push has left Cautious and Balanced on screen and pushed Hands-off under the caption scrim, its title greyed to the edge of legibility and its subtitle gone entirely. The sub-heading it was supposed to have DROPPED was still in frame and clipped mid-sentence at the right edge ('...do on its own' with no question mark), because the window was off-centre: 0.538 from x 0.131 centres on plate x 0.400 while the cards centre on 0.500.

That is the exact failure the old note said a 1.754x framing had been rejected for. It was not fixed by moving to 0.538; it was reproduced.

landscape 0.58 from (0.21, 0.269) — scale 2.225 against the old 2.398, so barely less zoom. Almost all of the fix is POSITION. Verified on a focus-preview end frame: all three cards whole, top border of Cautious clear of the frame edge, Hands-off's subtitle clear of the caption band, nothing clipped at either side, and the Back/Skip/Next row out of frame.

portrait 0.754 from (0.122, 0.246), scale 1.849. Portrait is the tighter constraint of the two and the geometry is worth writing down: the window can never start lower than 1-w, so clearing the sub-heading's second line (plate y 0.233) caps w at about 0.766, while the card text spans plate x 0.119-0.876 and wants about 0.80 to sit inside with margin. The two cannot both be satisfied. 0.754 takes the first: nothing is sliced, and the longest subtitle ('...auto-schedule estimate-bearing work') reaches the frame edge with its last glyph whole. Re-measure both when this rectangle moves.

POINTER. 'You choose' is a click, and the three cards are the control. It lands on Balanced in both cuts — landscape (0.500, 0.545), portrait (0.450, 0.540) — because Balanced is the option the plate shows SELECTED, teal border and all. Clicking Cautious or Hands-off would render a cursor pressing one card while a different one stays lit, which is the one way this pointer could contradict its own screenshot. Both hotspots are inside the NEW end windows (landscape 0.210-0.790 x 0.300-0.880; portrait 0.122-0.876 x 0.248-1.002) and inside the plate at rest, so the cursor tracks the control through the whole move; `ci-video check` resolves them and fails if it ever stops being true. Timing is left at the 58% default.
